title: Wastewater sampling and test procedures study guide
description: Study guide to 40 CFR 136.1-136.3: when Part 136 methods apply, alternate procedures, Table II containers, preservation and holding times.
intro: 40 CFR Part 136 sets the test procedures that must be used when pollutants are measured for NPDES applications and reports, State section 401 certifications, and sewage sludge permits and Part 503 records. This guide sets out what sections 136.1, 136.2 and 136.3 state on applicability and definitions, approved and alternate test procedures, Table II (required containers, preservation techniques and holding times) and its footnotes on grab and composite samples, when holding time begins, and requests for limited use changes. Many rules carry "except", "unless specified otherwise" or "under certain circumstances" conditions. Your State program and your facility's permit may have their own requirements, so check them too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

points.text: The Part 136 procedures must be used, except as noted in 136.4, 136.5 and 136.6, whenever the listed waste constituent is required to be measured for the purposes in 136.1(a).
points.quote: The procedures prescribed herein shall, except as noted in §§ 136.4, 136.5, and 136.6, be used to perform the measurements indicated whenever the waste constituent specified is required to be measured for:

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Those purposes include applications submitted to the Director and reports required under NPDES permits, and other requests for effluent data under parts 122 through 125.
points.quote: An application submitted to the Director and/or reports required to be submitted under NPDES permits or other requests for quantitative or qualitative effluent data under parts 122 through 125 of this chapter; and

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: They also include certifications issued by States under section 401 of the Clean Water Act.
points.quote: Certifications issued by States pursuant to section 401 of the Clean Water Act (CWA), as amended.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For sewage sludge, the procedures in Part 136 and in Part 503 must be used for measurements for a sewage sludge permit application under section 405(f) of the Clean Water Act and for Part 503 recordkeeping and reporting.
points.quote: The procedure prescribed herein and in part 503 of title 40 shall be used to perform the measurements required for an application submitted to the Administrator or to a State for a sewage sludge permit under section 405(f) of the Clean Water Act and for recordkeeping and reporting requirements under part 503 of title 40.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For the NPDES program, when more than one test procedure is approved for a pollutant, the procedure used must be sufficiently sensitive as defined in the Part 122 sections cited.
points.quote: For the purposes of the NPDES program, when more than one test procedure is approved under this part for the analysis of a pollutant or pollutant parameter, the test procedure must be sufficiently sensitive as defined at 40 CFR 122.21(e)(3) and 122.44(i)(1)(iv).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: In Part 136, "Director" has the meaning given in 40 CFR 122.2.
points.quote: Director means the director as defined in 40 CFR 122.2.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: NPDES is the national system for issuing permits under section 402 of the Act, and it includes any State or interstate program approved by the Administrator in whole or in part.
points.quote: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) means the national system for the issuance of permits under section 402 of the Act and includes any State or interstate program which has been approved by the Administrator, in whole or in part, pursuant to section 402 of the Act.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Detection limit is the minimum concentration of an analyte that can be measured and reported with 99% confidence that it is distinguishable from the method blank results, as determined by the procedure in appendix B to Part 136.
points.quote: Detection limit means the minimum concentration of an analyte (substance) that can be measured and reported with a 99% confidence that the analyte concentration is distinguishable from the method blank results as determined by the procedure set forth at appendix B of this part.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Approved test procedures and alternatives

points.text: Parameters with approved methods are listed, with test procedure descriptions and references, in Tables IA through IH of 136.3.
points.quote: Parameters or pollutants, for which methods are approved, are listed together with test procedure descriptions and references in Tables IA, IB, IC, ID, IE, IF, IG, and IH of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The full texts of Methods 601-613, 624.1, 625.1, 1613, 1624 and 1625 are printed in appendix A to Part 136, and Method 200.7 is printed in appendix C.
points.quote: The full texts of Methods 601-613, 624.1, 625.1, 1613, 1624, and 1625 are printed in appendix A of this part, and the full text of Method 200.7 is printed in appendix C of this part.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The procedure for determining the method detection limit is given in appendix B to Part 136.
points.quote: The full text for determining the method detection limit when using the test procedures is given in appendix B of this part.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If the reporting requirements of 40 CFR parts 122 and 125 conflict with reporting requirements tied to a listed method, parts 122 and 125 control and determine the permittee's reporting requirements.
points.quote: In the event of a conflict between the reporting requirements of 40 CFR parts 122 and 125 and any reporting requirements associated with the methods listed in these tables, the provisions of 40 CFR parts 122 and 125 are controlling and will determine a permittee's reporting requirements.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The date after a method number shows the latest editorial change of the method.
points.quote: The date after the method number indicates the latest editorial change of the method.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Under certain circumstances (paragraph (c) of 136.3, 136.5(a) through (d), or 40 CFR 401.13), other additional or alternate test procedures may be used.
points.quote: Under certain circumstances (paragraph (c) of this section, § 136.5(a) through (d) or 40 CFR 401.13,) other additional or alternate test procedures may be used.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Under certain circumstances, the Director may set discharge limits for a parameter that has no test procedure in Part 136 or in parts 405 through 499; the Director then specifies the test procedure.
points.quote: Under certain circumstances, the Director may establish limitations on the discharge of a parameter for which there is no test procedure in this part or in 40 CFR parts 405 through 499. In these instances the test procedure shall be specified by the Director.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Under certain circumstances, the Administrator may approve additional alternate test procedures for nationwide use, on the recommendation of the Alternate Test Procedure Program Coordinator in Washington, DC.
points.quote: Under certain circumstances, the Administrator may approve additional alternate test procedures for nationwide use, upon recommendation by the Alternate Test Procedure Program Coordinator, Washington, DC.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: The method tables IA to IH, their notes, and the material incorporated by reference in 136.3(b) are not set out here. Sections 136.4 to 136.6 (alternate test procedure applications and method modifications) are outside this set. Your State program and your facility's permit may have their own requirements, so check them too.

topics.name: Table II and limited use changes

points.text: Sample preservation procedures, container materials and maximum allowable holding times for the parameters in Tables IA to IH are prescribed in Table II.
points.quote: Sample preservation procedures, container materials, and maximum allowable holding times for parameters are cited in Tables IA, IB, IC, ID, IE, IF, IG, and IH are prescribed in Table II.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Information in Table II takes precedence over information in specific methods or elsewhere.
points.quote: Information in the table takes precedence over information in specific methods or elsewhere.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Any person may apply for a change from the prescribed preservation techniques, container materials and maximum holding times for samples taken from a specific discharge.
points.quote: Any person may apply for a change from the prescribed preservation techniques, container materials, and maximum holding times applicable to samples taken from a specific discharge.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Applications for these limited use changes may be made by letter to the Regional ATP Program Coordinator or the permitting authority in the Region where the discharge will occur.
points.quote: Applications for such limited use changes may be made by letters to the Regional Alternative Test Procedure (ATP) Program Coordinator or the permitting authority in the Region in which the discharge will occur.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The application should include enough data to show that the changes do not adversely affect the integrity of the sample.
points.quote: Sufficient data should be provided to assure such changes in sample preservation, containers or holding times do not adversely affect the integrity of the sample.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The Regional ATP Coordinator or permitting authority reviews the application and notifies the applicant and the appropriate State agency of approval or rejection.
points.quote: The Regional ATP Coordinator or permitting authority will review the application and then notify the applicant and the appropriate State agency of approval or rejection of the use of the alternate test procedure.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A decision on a request to deviate from the Table II requirements will be made within 90 days of receipt of the application by the Regional Administrator.
points.quote: requirements will be made within 90 days of receipt of the application by the Regional Administrator.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: An analyst may not modify the sample preservation or holding time requirements of an approved method unless the requirements of 136.3 are met.
points.quote: An analyst may not modify any sample preservation and/or holding time requirements of an approved method unless the requirements of this section are met.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: Table II itself is not reproduced; check the row for each parameter in the regulation.

points.text: In Table II, "P" means polyethylene and "FP" means fluoropolymer (PTFE or other fluoropolymer), unless Table II says otherwise.
points.quote: "P" is for polyethylene; "FP" is fluoropolymer (polytetrafluoroethylene [PTFE]; Teflon®), or other fluoropolymer, unless stated otherwise in this Table II

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: "G" means glass, "PA" means any sterilizable (autoclavable) plastic, and "LDPE" means low density polyethylene.
points.quote: "G" is glass; "PA" is any plastic that is made of a sterilizable material (polypropylene or other autoclavable plastic); "LDPE" is low density polyethylene.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Except where Table II and the method say otherwise, each grab sample must be preserved within 15 minutes of collection.
points.quote: Except where noted in this Table II and the method for the parameter, preserve each grab sample within 15 minutes of collection.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A composite sample collected with an automated sampler must be refrigerated at ≤6 °C during collection, unless Table II or the method specifies otherwise.
points.quote: For a composite sample collected with an automated sample (e.g., using a 24-hour composite sample; see 40 CFR 122.21(g)(7)(i) or 40 CFR part 403, appendix E), refrigerate the sample at ≤6 °C during collection unless specified otherwise in this Table II or in the method(s).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A composite sample to be split into aliquots must be kept at ≤6 °C, unless Table II or the method specifies otherwise, until collection, splitting and preservation are completed.
points.quote: For a composite sample to be split into separate aliquots for preservation and/or analysis, maintain the sample at ≤6 °C, unless specified otherwise in this Table II or in the method(s), until collection, splitting, and preservation is completed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The preservative is added to the container before collection when it will not compromise the integrity of a grab sample, a composite sample or an aliquot split from a composite sample within 15 minutes of collection.
points.quote: Add the preservative to the sample container prior to sample collection when the preservative will not compromise the integrity of a grab sample, a composite sample, or aliquot split from a composite sample within 15 minutes of collection.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If a composite measurement is required but a composite sample would compromise sample integrity, individual grab samples must be collected at prescribed time intervals, analyzed separately and the concentrations averaged.
points.quote: If a composite measurement is required but a composite sample would compromise sample integrity, individual grab samples must be collected at prescribed time intervals (e.g., 4 samples over the course of a day, at 6-hour intervals). Grab samples must be analyzed separately and the concentrations averaged.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: As an alternative, grab samples may be collected in the field and composited in the laboratory if the result equals arithmetic averaging of the individual grab sample results.
points.quote: Alternatively, grab samples may be collected in the field and composited in the laboratory if the compositing procedure produces results equivalent to results produced by arithmetic averaging of results of analysis of individual grab samples.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A sample shipped by common carrier or sent by the U.S. Postal Service must comply with the DOT Hazardous Materials Regulations; the person offering it for transportation is responsible for compliance.
points.quote: When any sample is to be shipped by common carrier or sent via the U.S. Postal Service, it must comply with the Department of Transportation Hazardous Materials Regulations (49 CFR part 172). The person offering such material for transportation is responsible for ensuring such compliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Aqueous samples must be preserved at ≤6 °C and should not be frozen unless data showing freezing does not harm sample integrity is kept on file and accepted as valid by the regulatory authority.
points.quote: Aqueous samples must be preserved at ≤6 °C, and should not be frozen unless data demonstrating that sample freezing does not adversely impact sample integrity is maintained on file and accepted as valid by the regulatory authority.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The preservation temperature does not apply to samples analyzed immediately (less than 15 minutes).
points.quote: The preservation temperature does not apply to samples that are analyzed immediately (less than 15 minutes).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Table II lists the Winkler dissolved oxygen sample in glass (bottle and top), fixed on site and stored in the dark.
points.quote: 47. Winkler G, Bottle and top Fix on site and store in dark

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Holding times

points.text: Samples should be analyzed as soon as possible after collection; the Table II times are the maximum times a sample may be held before the start of analysis and still be valid.
points.quote: Samples should be analyzed as soon as possible after collection. The times listed are the maximum times that samples may be held before the start of analysis and still be considered valid.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Samples may be held longer only if the permittee or monitoring laboratory has data on file showing the analytes are stable for the longer time for those sample types, and has received a variance from the Regional ATP Coordinator under 136.3(e).
points.quote: Samples may be held for longer periods only if the permittee or monitoring laboratory have data on file to show that, for the specific types of samples under study, the analytes are stable for the longer time, and has received a variance from the Regional ATP Coordinator under § 136.3(e).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For a grab sample, the holding time begins at the time of collection.
points.quote: For a grab sample, the holding time begins at the time of collection.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For a composite sample collected with an automated sampler, the holding time begins at the end of collection of the composite sample.
points.quote: For a composite sample collected with an automated sampler (e.g., using a 24-hour composite sampler; see 40 CFR 122.21(g)(7)(i) or 40 CFR part 403, appendix E), the holding time begins at the time of the end of collection of the composite sample.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For a set of grab samples composited in the field or laboratory, the holding time begins when the last grab sample in the set is collected.
points.quote: For a set of grab samples composited in the field or laboratory, the holding time begins at the time of collection of the last grab sample in the set.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Some samples may not be stable for the maximum time; a permittee or monitoring laboratory must hold a sample for a shorter time if it knows a shorter time is needed for stability.
points.quote: Some samples may not be stable for the maximum time period given in the table. A permittee or monitoring laboratory is obligated to hold the sample for a shorter time if it knows that a shorter time is necessary to maintain sample stability.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For a set of grab samples to be composited that is collected across two calendar dates, the date of collection is both dates (for example, November 14-15).
points.quote: For a set of grab samples to be composited, and that are collected across two calendar dates, the date of collection is the dates of the two days; e.g., November 14-15.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Table II lists total residual chlorine in P or G containers, no preservation required, analyzed within 15 minutes.
points.quote: 17. Chlorine, total residual P, G None required Analyze within 15 minutes.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: Holding times for each parameter are in the Table II rows; only examples are given here.

topics.name: Footnotes for specific tests

points.text: For the bacterial tests marked with footnote 22, analysis should begin as soon as possible after receipt, and incubation must be started no later than 8 hours from the time of collection.
points.quote: Sample analysis should begin as soon as possible after receipt; sample incubation must be started no later than 8 hours from time of collection.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For fecal coliform samples of sewage sludge (biosolids) only, the holding time is extended to 24 hours for Class A composted, Class B aerobically digested and Class B anaerobically digested samples, using EPA Method 1680 or 1681.
points.quote: For fecal coliform samples for sewage sludge (biosolids) only, the holding time is extended to 24 hours for the following sample types using either EPA Method 1680 (LTB-EC) or 1681 (A-1): Class A composted, Class B aerobically digested, and Class B anaerobically digested.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For the protozoan tests, holding time runs from collection to elution for samples shipped in bulk, and from filtration to elution for samples filtered in the field.
points.quote: Holding time is calculated from time of sample collection to elution for samples shipped to the laboratory in bulk and calculated from the time of sample filtration to elution for samples filtered in the field.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For dissolved metals, grab samples are filtered within 15 minutes of collection and before preservatives are added.
points.quote: For dissolved metals, filter grab samples within 15 minutes of collection and before adding preservatives.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Under footnote 19, an aqueous sample may be collected and shipped without acid preservation.
points.quote: An aqueous sample may be collected and shipped without acid preservation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The acid must then be added at least 24 hours before analysis, and immediately if the sample must be analyzed within 24 hours of collection.
points.quote: added at least 24 hours before analysis to dissolve any metals that adsorb to the container walls. If the sample must be analyzed within 24 hours of collection, add the acid immediately (see footnote 2).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A sample collected for total or dissolved trace level mercury must be analyzed within 90 days of collection.
points.quote: A sample that has been collected for determination of total or dissolved trace level mercury must be analyzed within 90 days of sample collection.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For toxicity samples, enough ice must be shipped so ice is still present on arrival, and the sample temperature must still be measured immediately on arrival.
points.quote: Place sufficient ice with the samples in the shipping container to ensure that ice is still present when the samples arrive at the laboratory. However, even if ice is present when the samples arrive, immediately measure the temperature of the samples and confirm that the preservation temperature maximum has not been exceeded.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Aqueous toxicity samples must not be frozen; hand-delivered samples used on the day of collection do not need to be cooled to 0 to 6 °C before the test starts.
points.quote: Aqueous samples must not be frozen. Hand-delivered samples used on the day of collection do not need to be cooled to 0 to 6 °C prior to test initiation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Orthophosphate samples are filtered immediately upon collection (within 15 minutes) to assess the dissolved or bio-available form.
points.quote: The immediate filtration requirement in orthophosphate measurement is to assess the dissolved or bio-available form of orthophosphorus (i.e., that which passes through a 0.45-micron filter), hence the requirement to filter the sample immediately upon collection (i.e., within 15 minutes of collection).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: The footnotes for organic compounds (8 to 15), cyanide (5 and 6) and hexavalent chromium (20) are not covered point by point.
